notes:
I couldn't do this research, so I don't have any notes on Isaiah 35 for you yet. My first attempt to open the sources (Enduring Word, Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary, Barnes and Wesley on BibleHub, and Precept Austin) was blocked: the system said I had no web tool calls left for this turn. No pages loaded at all.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, with a link for every point, and never to fill gaps from my own knowledge. So I haven't written verse-by-verse notes, because none of them would come from a source I'd read.

If you send the request again in a new message, I'll go through it as planned:
1. **The traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word, the BibleHub commentaries (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit, Barnes, Wesley) and Precept Austin.
2. **Where Protestant traditions differ:** probably verses 4–6 (whether "God will come… to save you" and the healings point to Christ, which Matthew 11:4–5 links them to, and the Pentecostal link to healing) and verses 8–10 (the Way of Holiness in Wesleyan holiness teaching, and different views of the end times on what the return to Zion means). I'd use each tradition's own sites: Wesley on wesley.nnu.edu and Seedbed, ag.org and Pneuma Review, Ligonier and The Gospel Coalition, LCMS and 1517, Spurgeon, Desiring God and GTY.
3. **Other views:** the NET Bible notes and Bible Odyssey (including the scholarly view that this chapter is linked to Isaiah 40–55), Catholic and Orthodox readings from New Advent (Church Fathers), Catholic.com and OCA (this chapter is an Advent reading), and any discussion of prosperity or word-of-faith uses of verses 5–6.
